title: the descriptor
text: What the minimal deformation descriptor $\xi_i$ is for the medium (a scalar is insufficient; the six-component form is the minimum that separates compression from shear) is not fixed by the sources.

title: independent $V_{\rm disp}$
text: A value of the exclusion volume from geometry and dynamics, not from the measured mass.

title: identification
text: That the vacuum *is* the corner-sharing network (CONDENSA, interpretive identification).

title: coordination and winding
text: Coordination 4 and $W+1=4$ are recorded together; no derivation connects them.

title: void fraction and R1
text: The diamond-limit node model has void fraction $0.66$; R1 states a gap-free medium. The sources do not reconcile the two, and Chapter 22 returns to the interstitial voids.

title: isotropy
text: The dispersion relation of the random hinge network, needed to show isotropic propagation at the measured level.

title: the term
text: *Dodecardinal* is defined only in a superseded Helix header (the 1+12 cuboctahedral set), and the engine applies the word to a different arrangement (the APS14 polar dyad and six-ring). This edition adopts the source definition and describes the engine's arrangement under its own name. Whether the physical medium's twelve contact directions are the cuboctahedral or the icosahedral set is the lattice fork of Chapter 1 and is open.

title: the centre crossing
text: The continuation of a trajectory through $r<\mathrm{Om}$, and the physical content of the arrest premise, are open (Chapter 53).

title: the pole
text: All conventions here are chart conventions. Whether a physical axis (a rotation axis) enters a statement is stated where it does; Chapter 58 treats the numerical conditioning at the poles and antipodes.

title: the exponents
text: The power of $1-z$ in the oscillator rate and in the closure is set to reproduce measured first-order coefficients (GOM22). A derivation from the contact mechanics is outstanding, and until it exists relations (3.4) are constrained by those measurements and do not predict them.

title: supersession
text: `Theory/00_Ruleset.md` lists T16 as $d\tau/dt=\sqrt{1-zR/r}$. The engine's active relation is $C=1-z$ (GOM22: the earlier form gave half the solar shift). The Ruleset text has not been updated, and the canon is edited only on the author's approval; the discrepancy is recorded here and in the supersession ledger.

title: dispersion
text: The medium's $\omega(\kappa)$, and with it the separation of phase, group and front speeds, is open (Chapter 14).

title: circulation
text: Conservation of $\Gamma$ in (3.3) is not established.

title: the second-order fork
text: The engine carries $c_{\rm far}=c(1-z)^2$ and the shared form $c(1-2z)$ as the two candidates; they agree to first order and differ at second order and in where the speed vanishes (Chapter 40).

title: the identification $z=\mathrm{Om}/r$
text: The engine's convergence-depth block and CONDENSA line 71 set the relay slowing equal to koppa over radius. The author ruled on 2026-11-03 that this is an error to be removed and that $z(r)$ must come out of the model. The canon is edited only on the author's approval, so the engine values (Table 3.3, Section 3.8) are reported as the engine's, not as derived; every later chapter that uses the engine's depth carries this label.

title: the constant $\kappa$
text: The value $\kappa = 1$ means the interception cross-section equals $\ell^2$. A cubic cell presents between $\ell^2$ (face-on) and $\sqrt3\,\ell^2$ (corner-on) and $\tfrac32\ell^2$ averaged over orientation. A value of $\kappa$ other than 1 rescales $P_{\rm conv}$ and every quantity downstream of it, including the transfer function $P_{\rm eff}/P_{\rm conv}$. A derivation of $\kappa$ from the geometry of the cell is outstanding. The exponent and the linear dependence on $N$ do not depend on it.

title: common or own domain
text: Section 4.6.

title: fidelity
text: Bound (4.15) is a requirement on the medium. A derivation that relay in the contact medium is faithful to that precision is outstanding; Chapter 14 returns to it.

title: the lattice
text: The lattice type fixes the $O(1)$ offset in (4.9) and the $O(d)$ term of the shell population; the choice of lattice for the contact medium is open.

title: Ruleset currency
text: The Ruleset's table lacks T18 and states the superseded T16. Proposed correction, pending approval: add the T18 row (Law VI, vortex topology quantisation) and replace the T16 expression by $d\tau/dt=1-z$ with its domain, citing the repair.

title: the numbering of T7–T9
text: The Ruleset and the Complete Laws paper assign different statements to 7, 8 and 9. A single numbering has not been chosen.

title: the boundary event
text: Operator (2) needs an accounting basis (energy, momentum, or both with signs); the engine implements no routine for the partition $\varepsilon\to(\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_t,\varepsilon_a)$ as such, and Chapter 15 sets up the ledger.

title: wake formation
text: Operator (4) is carried by two laws, and the multipole assignment ($\ell=1$ electric, $\ell=2$ magnetic, $\ell\ge3$ structure) is stated without a derivation in the Ruleset.

title: Law II
text: The release cascade has no numbered theorem; the statements it supports are corollaries.

title: the stored $\ell_P$
text: A derivation of the number from the c-boundary per baryon and the proton wake without the Planck-length definition is open; until then every quantity built on $N$ and $P_{\rm conv}$ carries CALIBRATED(1) through $\ell_P$.

title: $R_{\rm CMB}$
text: A value of the Clearing distance derived from the Law I chain without the $H_0$ input is open (CONDENSA §7).

title: legacy ballparks
text: Migration of the downstream tools off `T_rec` and `z_rec` is owed in the engine.

title: borrowed unit
text: The moments in `mu_*` need a native ratio (Chapter 24).

title: radiation constant digits
text: `a_rad` is stored to five digits, $4.4\times10^{-6}$ below the value computed from $k_B$, $h$, $c$; the shift propagates to $\varepsilon$, $\Phi$ and $P_{\rm conv}$ equally. A proposal to store more digits is canon work and waits for approval.

title: the one number of the seed
text: The sources do not state whether $\theta=1.9237\times10^{-32}$ is an input, an output of the cosmology, or a relation to $N$.

title: the quoted polynomial
text: The comment at `laws.hpp:2404` gives the polynomial of $T(2,5)$ for the $(2,3)$ mode. Proposed correction, pending approval: replace it by $t^{-1}-1+t$.

title: the mode lock
text: Why $v_T^2:v_P^2=p:q$, equivalently $R/a=\sqrt{q/p}$, is not derived. The open problem asks for a lattice calculation that solves the coupled mode equations and finds the discrete set of self-consistent $(R/a,\alpha)$ (`Theory/03_Open_Problems.md`, problem 1).

title: the stability spectrum
text: That only $W=1$ and $W=3$ are stable, and the lifetime of $W=2$, need a lattice reconnection calculation that supplies the resistance curve, the barrier and the dissipation law (open problem 2).

title: the identification
text: That the electron is $(1,1)$, the proton $(2,3)$ and the neutrino an open winding is the content of Law VI and is posited here.

title: the outgoing ledger
text: The outgoing channels of a reconnection are not modelled.

title: the state
text: The relay-response part of (8.1) is not specified by the sources. The descriptor of a cell is open (Chapter 1, R1.1).

title: existence and uniqueness
text: The engine's time-stepping routines come with no existence or uniqueness theorem. The relay-lock fraction is not Lipschitz at $r=0$ (Section 8.3).

title: event rules
text: Contact creation and change of winding class have no event rule that gives a unique continuation (Chapter 7, R7.3, R7.5).

title: the arrest exponents
text: No exponent $p$, $m_F$, $a$ or $b$ has been assigned to a physical state; (8.4) is a criterion and not a result (Chapter 53).

title: `step_locus` near the centre
text: The loss of accuracy of Table 8.3, and the proposed half-angle form.

title: momentum carried by content (P7)
text: That the content in transit carries momentum $(\text{energy})/c_{\rm relay}$, with the isotropic flux $q=U/4\pi$, is assumed here. It is not derived from the relay premises P1–P6, and the identification of $P_{\rm conv}$ with the density $U$ (rather than with a stress) is part of it. The investigation of 2026-10-27 records that the radiation pressure of the microwave background, $u_{\rm CMB}/3$, is not the same quantity as $P_{\rm conv}=Nu_{\rm CMB}$.

title: the boundary response of matter (P8)
text: Propositions 9.1 and 9.3 show that the traction and the sphere force depend on how a surface returns the content. For the Law III coefficient $\pi/4$ to be universal across Coulomb, gravity and nuclear forces, the effective response must be the same, absorbing or specular, in all three. A derivation of the response of a persistent form from its structure is outstanding.

title: common or own domain
text: Whether any anisotropy exists (Section 9.5) depends on residual R4.2.

title: which factor Law IV needs
text: The engine's resistance law uses $P_{\rm conv}/3$, the specular value (9.6) and the trace share of $\Pi$. The traction on an absorbing boundary of the engaged volume is $P_{\rm conv}/6$. Which of the two, or an intermediate $(1+\rho)/6$, belongs to the boundary of the engaged volume is not fixed by Law IV's premises; Chapter 12 returns to it. The Ruleset's T7 states $\tau=1/3$ as the normal projection of the isotropic tensor, which is (9.4) and (9.6) and not (9.5).

title: symbol use
text: $P_{\rm conv}$ names $\Phi/\ell^3$ in the engine and $\Phi/3\ell^3$ in Corollary 3.2 of the Complete Laws (Section 9.3).

title: operator-level account
text: The responses of Sections 9.4 and 9.6 borrow the vocabulary of radiation pressure. A statement of the force in operator terms (the relay operator of a spation against the exclusion and circulation of a particle), with no absorption, is outstanding; the coefficients $U/6$, $U/3$, $\pi/4$ are properties of the geometry under the stated responses and survive only as far as such an account reproduces them.

title: the response model
text: Proposition 10.1 holds for an absorbing or specular target (Chapter 9, R9.6). A diffusely scattering target changes the coefficient (Chapter 9, Proposition 9.3), and an operator-level account of the response is outstanding.

title: many bodies
text: The exact pair result does not extend by addition. Overlapping shadows (Section 10.6) and shielding of one pair by a third body need the union measure; the quantitative treatment is Chapter 35.

title: non-spherical forms
text: The proton's trefoil and any nucleus are not spheres; the orientation-dependent overlap of (10.4) has not been computed for them.

title: the seven-circle model
text: The model covers $7/9$ of a body's outline and assigns weights that sum to 1; the relation between the geometry and the weights is a modelling choice, not a derivation.

title: contact
text: The identity (10.5) is exact to contact for hard spheres. For the boundary radii of atomic and nuclear forms ($R_p$, $r_e$) the separations of interest are many orders of magnitude beyond contact, and what happens at contact for forms whose boundaries are equilibria (Chapter 18) is not settled.

title: the electropause derivation
text: The route from the balance of EMC04 to (11.3) and the FLM07 premise are not reproduced here; the engine records the form as class C conditional on that premise.

title: supersession
text: The Complete Laws paper (Section 4.2) states $Z^2$ scaling for He$^+$; the engine uses $Z$.

title: the sign
text: The handed redirection that gives repulsion its sign has no derivation in this book, and the engine states a magnitude only.

title: the gravity class
text: The pressure that goes with the per-body-radii form for real boundaries, and the ratio of the gravitational and electric couplings, are not executed here; they enter through the c-boundary in Chapters 33–36.

title: which radius
text: The measured $R_p$ and the lock boundary differ by $0.02\%$, which is $0.04\%$ in the force at the Bohr radius; the scope of each use is stated where it occurs.

title: a stale comment
text: The engine's comment at the transfer function gives $2.125\times10^{-17}$; the executed value is $2.1242\times10^{-17}$.

title: momentum of the content
text: P7 is assumed (Chapter 9, R9.1); the derivation of (12.2) rests on it.

title: two dipoles
text: The Complete Laws state the first-order dipole of the arrival twice, with coefficients that differ by a factor 2 (Eq. 3.1 and Corollary 7.1), and the Corollary's distribution does not return $\gamma$. A single statement of the distribution, with its derivation, is outstanding. If the Corollary's dipole were the correct one, every $V_{\rm disp}$ obtained from a measured mass would halve.

title: an independent exclusion volume
text: A $V_{\rm disp}$ from geometry and dynamics without the target mass (Chapter 1, R1.2).

title: equivalence
text: The identity of inertial and gravitational mass needs the shadow of a body to be set by its $V_{\rm disp}$; the two proton volumes of the engine differ by $10^{13}$ (Chapter 49).

title: which share
text: The share 1/3 against 1/6 for the boundary of the engaged volume (Chapter 9, R9.4) changes every exclusion volume by a factor 2.

title: first order
text: The derivation is first order in $v/c$; the speed limit from the trailing hemisphere extrapolates it to $v=c$.

title: scope of orthogonality
text: The budget equality $v_{\rm circ}^2+v^2=c^2$ is axiom M3 (posited). Pointwise orthogonality of the circulation and translation velocities is not true of every tangent of a general closed path; the mode-averaged form (13.3) needs a derived weight.

title: the persistence action
text: The derivation of $E$ and $\vec p$ in (13.20)–(13.25) uses constant action per local cycle, a premise additional to the budget.

title: transverse extent
text: Longitudinal contraction follows from round-trip closure; the transverse extent and the density response (13.7) are not derived.

title: depth composition
text: The identification $z=\mathrm{Om}/r$ (Chapter 3, R3.6) and the rule for composing translation with depth (factorised or additive) are open.

title: two sources for $\gamma$
text: In this book $\gamma$ is obtained from the budget (13.9); it does not rest on Corollary 7.1 of the Complete Laws, whose distribution does not return $\gamma$ (Chapter 12, R12.2).

title: the radiative branch
text: The joint limit (13.51) is a controlled mathematical limit; the conversion dynamics that realise it are not given.

title: an engine surface
text: The optional-locus return of the spherical response cannot distinguish a zero vector, a rejected state and an unavailable result (Section 13.17, item 7).

title: the response operator
text: $K_{ab}$ of the real medium is not known; the chain is a TOY.

title: polarisation
text: The shear response that would give transverse modes, and their speeds, are not specified.

title: the reversal fraction
text: The physical origin of $s$ in the contact medium, and its value at observed wavenumbers, are open. The chain bounds it from above by the existence of waves at all (Section 14.5).

title: energy velocity
text: The ratio of transported energy flux to stored energy density has not been computed for the chain.

title: the epoch branch
text: The lookback and loading branches of the acoustic relation belong to the Spaz chapters.

title: the acoustic input
text: $R_{\rm load}$ enters from outside; the relation is the engine's.

title: the scatterer of the chain
text: The agent that takes the recoil (15.2) is not specified in the TOY chain.

title: the medium term for real bodies
text: Whether bodies exchange momentum with the relay medium, and how much, is not computed. The engine has no such term, so its closure (15.4) is a statement about the kernel. A computation of the medium's transport that is independent of the requirement of balance is owed.

title: the pair term of the energy
text: The engine does not say whether the pair term in (15.4) corresponds to content stored anywhere. Its relation to the energy of Chapter 13 is not derived here.

title: one length for source and weight
text: The equality of the source strength and the weight of $\vec P$ in the engine is the weak-equivalence premise of Chapter 12; it is not derived in this chapter.

title: contact
text: The engine refuses a step at contact; the interaction through contact is not given here (Chapters 21 and 22).

title: circular-orbit test
text: The registered energy-order test was placed on a symmetric orbit and failed for a reason of symmetry (Section 15.5); the corrected test is on an eccentric orbit. The corrected criterion was fixed before it was coded and is recorded in the pre-registration.

title: the limit is of a TOY
text: The telegraph system is the scaling limit of a chain whose response operator is not that of the real medium (R14.1). The continuity and balance equations of the real medium are owed to a response law.

title: uniformity
text: The limits hold at first order and for $k\varepsilon\ll1$; behaviour near the hop scale is that of the chain.

title: relaxation count
text: The engine's transport kernel gives parabolic coefficients without a relaxation count; the crossover to the hyperbolic regime for the real medium is not given.

title: the thermal input
text: $T$ enters through $k_BT$ with $k_B$ a unit bridge; what $T$ measures in the relay medium is not derived here.

title: boundary and load from outside
text: The mechanical boundary $b$ and the load $m$ enter as inputs. No comparison with measured transport coefficients is made in this chapter; the engine's own comparison is its benchmark B16, and a registered comparison with measured coefficients is owed to the chapters that compare with measurement.

title: domain
text: The kernel is valid for the dilute monatomic hard-lock domain only, as the engine's header states.

title: the moments
text: The coefficients $\tfrac38,\tfrac5{16},\tfrac{75}{64}$ and the fraction $\tfrac67$ are taken from the engine; a derivation within the book is not given.

title: the construction operator
text: The operator $T[X]$ of the electron construction, its linearisation, $M_{\rm eff}$ and $K_{\rm eff}$ are not supplied by the engine. The stability of the persistent circulation is not established.

title: the effective coordinate
text: Which coordinate $q$ carries the small oscillation, and how Law IV's engaged displacement fixes $M_{\rm eff}$ for it, is not computed.

title: the rung
text: That $\alpha$ is hydrogen's koppa rung is a premise (derivelist); the identities of Section 17.2 are shared-input and do not test it.

title: external response
text: Polarisation, scattering and transition observables are not computed.

title: the spectral radius
text: An operationally inferred spectral radius is not entered: it requires a spectral observable and its inference chain.

title: beyond the point kernel
text: The route closure at $p=2$ holds for the point-source kernel; finite size, the movement budget (Chapter 13) and the response of the construction can shift it.

title: the price law
text: That the lock selects the lowest $q\rho^3$ is the engine's FLM07 premise; the geometry of the voids is verified, the pricing is not derived here.

title: pre-selection
text: That $q$ was fixed before the comparison with a radius is documented in the engine header and is not independently observable.

title: the uncertainty
text: The stored $R_p$ has no uncertainty, so the engine's falsification clause cannot be evaluated; the operational definitions of the lock radius and the measured radius differ (Section 18.4).

title: response
text: Stability, scattering and excitation of the proton are not computed.

title: the wake length
text: The closure (18.5) is an inverse evaluation; the independent determination of $\ell_P$ is owed.

title: the anisotropy
text: The rank-four anisotropy (18.2) is a prediction with no measurement.

title: barrier and rate
text: The barrier, the populations and the transition operator for a conversion are not supplied; no lifetime is computed.

title: spectrum and coupling
text: The spectrum and coupling rule of the open-winding channel are not supplied; the electron energy distribution within the allowed range is not fixed.

title: the channel's absolute scale
text: The stored mass values are conventions; their effect on the endpoint is below $10^{-7}Q$.

title: the medium term
text: $\Delta p_{\rm medium}=0$ is a decision of the ledger (an isolated complete region); whether the real medium exchanges momentum in a conversion (Chapter 15, R15.2) is not computed.

title: the capacity function
text: `contact_capacity` exceeds the exact maximum for $\max(Z,N)<3$; proposed correction $\min(3Z,3N,ZN)$, not applied.

title: the fate of lost contacts
text: Where the energy and momentum of the lost contacts go, and the barrier to re-forming them, are not computed.

title: embedded final states
text: The final states available to an embedded conversion depend on its seat; only the contact bookkeeping is executed.

title: coordinate versus module
text: That the module counts correspond to modules that can be built under the contact rule is not shown by the arithmetic; it is the subject of Chapters 21–24.

title: stability and table membership
text: The embedded table lists natural nuclides including radioactive primordial species; membership is not a stability classification.

title: fission
text: The identities (20.4) fix the change in module counts for a given $\nu$; they give no split probability and no mechanism.

title: the choice of base
text: The alpha base for $Z\ge2$ and the helion base for helium-3 are conventions of the construction; hydrogen-1 and hydrogen-2 are outside both.

title: the range
text: The table ends at $Z=92$; the grammar is stated beyond it but not embedded.

title: the rule's origin
text: The cap of three, and the exclusion of like contacts, are stated rules. The four-neighbour star shows the cap does not follow from equal-sphere packing.

title: realised contacts
text: How many of the slack contacts a given nucleus fills is not fixed by capacity.

title: orientation
text: The checker tests distances only; orientation compatibility, loop-length constraints and circulation are not tested.

title: the engine's capacity function
text: `contact_capacity` equals (21.1) except for $(1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2)$ (R19.5; proposal, not applied).

title: rigidity
text: Solid spheres are assumed; deformable boundaries (Chapter 22) change the geometry checks.

title: the onset
text: The pricing rule that selects $n=3$ is open; a derivation that does not use the closure list is owed.

title: polyhedral shells beyond $n=5$
text: The link counts for $n\ge6$ exceed the polyhedral edge bound; the contact topology of $D_{42}$ and later is unresolved.

title: closing contraction
text: The closing tightening of a triton shell is not reproduced; the missing degrees of freedom are not identified.

title: shared counting
text: The sequence of closures cannot discriminate from the prevailing account at the counting level.

title: the forward value
text: $N=184$ is a formula extension; no observation is recorded.

title: the functional
text: No energy functional of the contact law is available; restoring modes, barriers and binding residuals are not computed.

title: beyond the contact count
text: What fixes the energy per contact (orientation, compression, circulation) is open; the gear-frequency form needs a computed $\Delta\omega$ for the four configurations.

title: repricing
text: Reorganisation can reprice surviving contacts (the thermal analysis TD05 of the sources gives a warning of this kind); it was not re-run here.

title: the typed alpha value
text: The stored $B_\alpha$ is rounded to five digits ($1.4\times10^{-5}$ relative above the nuclear-mass value).

title: radius definitions
text: The bulk-law radius, the contact diameter and the measured radius are different operational quantities; they are not identified.

title: engine-recorded results
text: The NP05 exclusion and the 908-radius comparison are cited from the engine's records and not re-run.

title: labels and rule
text: No spin, parity or moment label is stored for the 287 records; a prediction needs sourced labels, a frozen configuration and a rule declared beforehand.

title: weights
text: The weights of a response moment (which units source the moment, with what strength) are not given by the geometry; the unit weights used here are a CONSTRUCTION.

title: units
text: The stored moments are in nuclear magnetons; a native ratio is not available.

title: population
text: The orientation distribution of a populated total-impulse state is not given.

title: circulation phase
text: Parity needs the phase of the circulation under inversion, which a point set does not carry.

title: the rotation-field function
text: No $Z$ argument; for $Z>1$ it is the ladder speed over $\sqrt Z$. Proposal: $c\alpha\sqrt{Za_0/r}$. Not applied.

title: the line list
text: The engine's ppm figures are not reproduced; the size of the omitted term at large $Z$ is not reconciled with them.

title: isotope shifts
text: The predicted shifts are not compared with measured shifts.

title: a native depth
text: An independent spectroscopic depth and circulation speed, which would make $zk^2=1$ a test, are not available.

title: the stability of the ladder
text: Persistence of each rung needs a restoring response (Chapter 17, R17.1); the identities above do not supply it.

title: the recurrence seat
text: The seat $J_1$ is taken from the stored set; deriving it from contact mechanics is owed.

title: stability and selection
text: Stability of each rung and the exclusion of competing modes are not derived for the electron construction (R17.1); no selection rule or transition operator is supplied.

title: the leading-order domain
text: Corrections of order $(Z\alpha/n)^2$ are omitted (Chapter 27).

title: the epoch
text: The varying-pressure conversion is not executed here.

title: the $l$-dependence
text: The operator that converts the scale (27.1) into a state-dependent splitting is not supplied.

title: hyperfine coefficient
text: The coupling $A$ needs the overlap and transfer calculation and a frozen nuclear geometry.

title: finite-size coefficient
text: The near-core exposure of each mode is not computed.

title: ordering
text: The ordering of hyperfine and finite-size contributions is not determined by power counting (ratio 115).

title: measured splittings
text: No measured line or splitting is loaded; all line residuals are owed.

title: selection and coupling
text: The overlap and coupling strength of the real circulation, the density of outgoing modes and so the rate of a transition are not derived; the harmonic content above is a classical route property.

title: the response kernel
text: The causal kernel of the real atom (poles, damping) is not supplied; $\Gamma$ is a parameter here.

title: the medium term
text: Reorganisation of the medium in an emission is set to zero in the ledger.

title: measured widths
text: No measured width, lifetime or angular distribution is loaded; the determining test needs line centres, widths, angular emission and excitation dependence from one mode coupling, with instrument broadening specified separately.

title: range
text: At most ten electrons; no periodic structure beyond neon.

title: seat order and form
text: The seat order, the form (29.1) and the claim that the pair prices are exact geometry are the engine's; they are not derived in this chapter.

title: multiple minima
text: The energy has two or more distinct minima for $Z\ge3$; global minimality is established by multi-start search only.

title: sign pattern
text: The signs of the residuals in Table 29.1 are not explained.

title: protocol
text: Relaxed and vertical ionisation differ by up to $4.5$ eV in the executed range; the comparison protocol has to be fixed per observable.

title: observables beyond ionisation
text: Radii, occupancy and excitation are not compared.

title: the map
text: No map $F$ from nuclear to atomic quantities with derived factors exists; none is proposed here.

title: isotope structure
text: Nuclear-structure dependent isotope shifts and moment changes are not predicted; seated configurations and sourced labels for a chain are owed.

title: higher rank
text: Possible correspondences at rank 4 and above are not tested.

title: time scales
text: Nuclear and electronic degrees of freedom have different time scales; the correspondence of frequencies $s_\nu$ is not addressed.

title: directions only
text: The atomic sets were compared by directions with equal weights; the radii of the shells (Chapter 29) and the weights of a response moment (Chapter 24, R24.2) are not included.

title: the bond mechanism
text: The bond-well functional is not supplied; the CH07 history (inverse well; rolling wall) leaves curvature and depth unclosed.

title: a native stiffness
text: Stiffness and depth must come from one contact law; the engine provides neither for molecules.

title: reaction rates
text: Mode populations, coupling and transport of released excitation are not computed.

title: measured constants
text: No measured equilibrium distance, frequency, isotope shift or dissociation energy is loaded; the determining comparison is owed.

title: a constitutive law
text: No stiffness tensor, equation of state or thermal law follows from the engine's contact law; the material rows are owed.

title: one order variable
text: The same order variable and energy ledger across a transition have not been specified.

title: dense transport
text: Closures for dense phases and internal modes are not derived.

title: rates
text: Nucleation, yielding and fracture rates need barriers and mode populations, not computed here.

title: measured materials
text: No measured modulus, latent heat or diffusivity is loaded.

title: what the similarity is
text: The relations are identities at one point; the empirical content is the constancy of $\mathrm{Om}$ and the agreement of independent determinations, established here to $1.4\times10^{-3}$ (planets) and $1\%$ (Earth).

title: joint response law
text: Whether a widening $\mathrm{Om}$ slows $v$ depends on the response of $c$, not supplied.

title: perturbations
text: The source lengths of the planets and the Moon, and the processing of the mean elements, are not separated from the spread.

title: hydrogen
text: The ladder is shared-input; an independent spectroscopic depth is not available.

title: the axis
text: The transition to vanishing transverse extent is not computed.

title: the departure
text: Which departure from the inverse-square source condition the real medium has is not determined here; $\kappa/r^3$ is a stand-in.

title: extended and moving sources
text: The conserved ledger is stated for a point source of fixed strength; extended, moving and history-dependent sources are treated in Chapter 35.

title: measured orbits
text: No measured trajectory is compared; the apsidal signature is a map for later comparison (Chapter 36).

title: the model
text: The seven-circle weights are a boundary model, not a derived cubature; why the uncovered area goes to the outer six is a choice of the model.

title: near contact
text: The disc quadrature loses accuracy inside about $0.5R$; the force near contact needs another representation.

title: edge sensitivity
text: A model error of order $0.02$ in the occluded fraction at an edge is not a limit on the force error for a moving blocker; the full pairwise force near an occultation is not computed.

title: the implementations
